projects.name: IFAD’s Maket Bilong Vilis Fama (MVF) aims at improving the livelihoods of village farming households in the target provinces, by facilitating their transition from semi-subsistence agriculture to market-oriented production and farming as a business. The project’s development goal is to achieve sustainable increased returns to village farming households from increased marketed production
projects.description:
The MVF project started in 2018 and was originally expected to end in 2024. The project recently received additional financing and was extended, with new expected completion date in September 2029.

The project will predominately focus on the fresh produce sub-sector which involves approximately 94% of village farmers across PNG. In addition, the project provide limited investment to pilot activities focused on stimulating the development of the galip nut value chain as this has potential to be become a new export cash crop for village farmers in PNG. 

The project was recently expanded to target seven provinces of PNG. Activities related to the fresh produce sub-sector will be implemented in four provinces in the Highlands Region (Western Highlands, Jiwaka, Simbu and Eastern Highlands) and one province in the Momase Region, Morobe. Galip nut related activities will be implemented in East New Britain, Madang and Morobe. Building on its initial success, the MVF was scaled up and now targets around 40,000 farming households, benefiting approximately 200,000 people.

projects.name: Pandemic F-Consolidating One Health approach for pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response PNG
projects.description: With the increase of international trade in recent years in PNG has also increased risk pathways for transboundary animal and plants exotic diseases and pests. The threats and risk are further compounded by climate changes, shifts in agricultural practices and changes in human ecology and behaviour. According to the National Agriculture Development Plan 2007-2016 states that “although, PNG is currently relatively free of the major pest and diseases; it faces major challenges to the sustainability of our agriculture and resources base in particular with the emerging issues relating to zoonosis, and other animal and plant pests and diseases.” In PNG, there has been no official reports of any major zoonotic disease or events since 2017 for the suspected anthrax outbreak in 2018 in Madang Province which affected thousands of pigs, although this was not confirmed. Over Over the years, there were surveys done on Leptospirosis in cattle farms and abattoirs in 2003-2006, and Bovine brucellosis detection survey in PNG (2010-2013). The five-priority zoonotic disease in PNG include foodborne zoonosis, zoonotic arbovirus, leptospirosis, anthrax, brucellosis, bovine tuberculosis, trichinellosis, Hydatid disease and cysticercosis. Although rabis has never been reported or detected in PNG, recent collaborative work has identified potential high-risk pathways for incursion into PNG along the land border. Risk assessment has also shown that current conditions in PNG are conducive for the spread of rabis if it entered PNG. According to the Global Health System Index Scoring report that was conducted by Word Health Organization (WHO) in collaboration with all sectors, the risk pathways and spread of zoonotic and transboundary disease and pest is very high in PNG, with pre-border, border and post border surveillance and quarantine system needing strengthening and capacity building to for proper regulatory and monitoring system. According to the two Evaluation Reports including WOAH, Performance Veterinary Services (PVS) Evaluation Report 2015 and WOAH Performance Veterinary Services (PVS) Veterinary Legislation Identification Mission Report, 2015 highlighted the gaps in the Veterinary services and animal health sector in PNG such as lack of veterinary and para-veterinary officials in PNG. The National Agriculture Quarantine and Inspection Authority (NAQIA) is the veterinary authority in PNG, as well as the mandated quarantine and boarder service provider. The number of veterinarians in PNG is less than 10, with three nationals and the balance made up of expatriates, with 50% providing veterinary services by the private sector. Hence, there is a need for more capacity building in the workforce in animal health and para-veterinary courses to help boost the workforce. In addition, the diagnostics capacity of the laboratory services for exotic disease for both plant and animal are minimal, lacking infrastructure as well as work force labour. There is need to strengthen the laboratory capacity for serology, PCR, AST, residual testing and microbiology culture, identification, and diagnosis. In 2019, FAO conducted the Assessment of the National Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance System (ATLASS) in food and agriculture sectors.  From the findings, the AMR Surveillance system of PNG was assessed to be at a country stage 1 (Limited capacity) on the progressive Improvement pathway (PIP). PNG has the capability to advance to PIP stage 2 and needs to train staff for Antimicrobial Sensitive testing (AST), develop standardized/harmonized methods for AST, improve equipment and reagent availably for AST, obtain bacteria through AMR surveillance for AST, and develop data management system for AMR information.The Surveillance, Laboratory capacity and human resources/workforce strengthening are the tree priority areas for PNG that need for strengthening, boosting and expanding.

projects.name: Support to the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) Policy 2015–2030 - Part 2
projects.description:
The proposed Action will directly support the implementation of the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Policy 2015 - 2030, as well as other targets, as stated in the Vision 50, the Development Strategic Plan 2010 - 2030, the Water Papua New Guinea Master Plan 2012 - 2030, the Medium Term Development Plan III 2018 - 2022, and ultimately contribute to the following Sustainable Development Goals: SDG 3, SDG 4, SDG 5, SD6, SDG 11, SDG 13.

3.1 The Action (project) objectives

In line with the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Policy (WaSH) 2015 - 2030, the proposed Action aims to contribute towards improving the quality of life of Papua New Guineans through increased access to and utilization of a safe, adequate and sustainable water supply, sanitation and improved hygiene practices.

General objective: The general objective of the Action is to improve the quality of life of women, children and men through contributing to increased access to safe, adequate and sustainable water supply and sanitation in locations of higher human concentration (schools, healthcare facilities, and major market places).

The project aims to achieve increased equitable access to safe, convenient and sustainable water supply and sanitation and improved hygiene practices and long-term hygiene behavior change at the personal, household, community and institutional level, particularly to urban areas that are currently under-served, in- line with the National WaSH policy. Hence, the specific objectives of the action are:

Specific Objective 1: Improved equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water in selected urban areas, focusing on vulnerable groups and locations of higher human concentration (schools, healthcare facilities, markets).

Specific Objective 2: Improved adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene in selected urban areas, with a special focus on locations of higher human concentrations (schools, healthcare facilities, markets) and paying special attention to the needs of women and girls and those in vulnerable situations, including improved nutrition for children in schools.

This reiterates the interventions' work towards increasing equity of services in urban towns/areas, and to disadvantaged groups, as well as reducing economic and financial losses related to accessing safe and sustainable water supply.

projects.name: National Health Facility Assessment Tool and related Capacity Development (#24589-0010
projects.description:
UNOPS with its expertise in construction implementation, condition assessment and development of infrastructure solutions is well placed to offer support to the NDoH and provincial and district levels in the development of capacity to carry out infrastructure audits and field assessments. Further, UNOPS holds expertise in the area of institutional capacity development, training and knowledge transfer and data management, analysis and visualization.
The main objective of the proposed project is to develop a rapid assessment tool for use at district level to capture information on the status of health facilities focusing on human resources, services and infrastructure and support the development of capacity in the use and application of this tool. The assessment tool will focus initially on Provincial Hospitals (Level 5), Rural and District Hospitals (Level 4)  and a selected number of Urban and Rural Health Centre (Level 3), capturing concise foundational data commensurate with the assigned level and facility type. 
The project will be implemented in a duration of 3 years commencing June 2024, with a proposed budget of AUD 9,217,223.

projects.name: Assessment of Community Health Centers - Impact Health Proj#24245-001
projects.description:
UNOPS is to provide expert services to the World Bank in supporting the National Department of Health (NDOH) with options and recommendations for a national health facility audit. The primary focus is on designing and piloting the audit in East New Britain Province, with the possibility of supporting subsequent phases. The tasks include developing standardized tools for the Health Facility Audit (HFA), aligning with National Health Service Standards (NHSS) and other priorities. The audit tools should be designed in collaboration with a firm creating a digital tool for data collection and organization.

The detailed audit areas cover various aspects, such as basic facility information, physical space, engineering standards, waste management, medical equipment, ICT, transportation, safety, staff housing, maternity waiting houses, and disability accessibility. The audit should be gender and inclusion responsive, and the design and content of the tools will be discussed and agreed upon with the World Bank and NDOH’s Facility Audit Technical Working Group.

Additionally, a desk review will be conducted, building on existing tools and information, including data from national databases. The consultant will conduct a detailed audit of Level 2-4 government and church-owned facilities in East New Britain, identifying gaps and quantifying requirements. The findings will allow for the quantification and costing of gaps, including conceptual level designs. The consultant will advise on immediate investment priorities, considering major infrastructure, safety issues, human resource capacity, and services related to reproductive, maternal, and child health.

Furthermore, the consultant will work with NDOH and Provincial Health Authority (PHA) to advise on recommendations for immediate investment priorities. The discussion on recommendations will include a consultative process to ensure understanding and transparency regarding criteria and trade-offs. The consultant will identify and advise on Environment and Social Management requirements and documentation for the IMPACT Health Project. The available budget for East New Britain is approximately US$1.75 million, subject to review.

Lastly, the development of capacity at NDOH and PHA is deemed important for the assignment, and joint collaboration is encouraged in both the design and field audit processes.

projects.name: Buka Electricity Grid Solar Upgrade - MFAT Funded Project
projects.description:
UNOPS initiated the Sustainable Energy Project for Buka as part of the Strengthening Infrastructure System in PNG. The Buka Electricity Grid Solar Upgrade aims to strengthen energy access for the Buka population through providing practical solar PV energy systems and upgrading the distribution systems, thereby enhancing the access to basic services and fostering economic development. The proposed project is expected to reduce reliance on expensive diesel generation by 90% and significantly improve the reliability and resilience of the Buka Island
electrical grid by meeting the existing and anticipated ten-year future demand.
The project outputs include:
An energy generation system comprising solar PV subsystem, BESS subsystem, backup generators, protection panel systems, communication control and energy management systems to manage the various power generation units and battery storage system to balance supply and demand; and An upgraded distribution system comprising step-up and step-down transformers, and other components necessary to rehabilitate the existing medium voltage (MV) distribution system and provide smart energy meters.

projects.name: Project Management Support for the Rural Public Service Delivery Project
projects.description:
The objective of the RSDP is to enhance communities' access to basic infrastructure and services in selected rural areas through inclusive and participatory planning and implementation. The project operates in five provinces (Central, East New Britain, Simbu, West Sepik, and Western) and was designed to benefit approximately 400,000 people.  
The project consists of three (3) main components:
Preparation and Implementation of Sub-Projects
Capacity Building of National and Sub-National Entities
Project Management
By utilising a CDD approach, the RSDP empowers communities to take an active role in their development, fostering ownership, accountability, and sustainability of the projects. This inclusive and participatory method ensures that the interventions are well-suited to the unique needs and priorities of each community, leading to more effective and lasting improvements in rural infrastructure and services.
The RSDP project will be delivered in alignment with Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) own development plans in close conjunction with the Government-owned Department of Provincial and Local-level Government Affairs (DPLGA). 
Following different constraints encountered on the project such as outbreak of covid, cash flow, logistic problems constraint, weather condition and security problem, it has become necessary to extent the service from May 31, 2024 to December 31, 2024 to ensure the sub-projects implementation can be fully completed and sustainability within the community.
